This site was built with coding agents, working from a brief and a run of
corrections.
This page is what I asked for and what I said back.
The [JuliaCon 2026 site](https://samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/prompts.html)
did the same, and the [how I LLM](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-I-llm) deck
before it put its prompt on a slide.

## The brief

This is my opening prompt, cleaned up for spelling and sentence boundaries and
grouped under headings.
The judgements are unchanged.
The verbatim version, typos and all, is
[in the repo][orig].
It began with the workshop programme and the organisers' request, which are
on the talk pages.

[orig]: https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/blob/main/notes/original-brief.md

### The site

::: {.prompt}
I am a bit confused as to what to put.
In the first instance I want you to use agents to create a folder in seabbs
like I did for JuliaCon 2026, AIandIDVUB, with the same structure.
I want the slides with their titles and QR codes and so on in place, but not
at this stage content.
Then I will make a matching GitHub repo and give access that you can push to.
I think we can have the abstract be what the ask was, in bullets.
:::

### The research

::: {.prompt}
Can you use agents to search my recent work for related work?
I am a bit confused if they mean agentic AI, deep learning, UDEs, or what, to
be honest.
:::

### The keynote

::: {.prompt}
Before I looked back at what they were talking about I was thinking of
giving a few sections in the first talk.
The first being a 10 minute intro to outbreak infectious disease modelling
over the last 10 years or so that I have been in the field: Ebola in West
Africa, awareness of and work done by others, then COVID, mpox, and the
current Ebola outbreak.
Then 10 minutes on agentic AI, how I LLM, which I have some stuff on, but
also what it means for modelling.
Then maybe 10 minutes on opportunities for other AI models: UDEs, PINNs,
neural flows for fitting (nfidd had a little on both of these, but high
level), foundation models for outbreaks and infectious disease forecasting
spinning out of current foundation time series models, agentic model
composition, i.e. Google's forecasting success with FluSight?
:::

### The communication lecture

::: {.prompt}
For communication, really not sure.
Can you mine my recent work and give a proposal?
:::

### How it should look

::: {.prompt}
In recent talks, look at the git history to see how I have pruned and
refined language and style to make it my own, and follow that.
Be wary of overly dense text on slides.
We like schematics, pictures and sparse clean slides.
:::

## How it was built

Five research agents ran first, before any slide was written, and wrote
their notes into
[`notes/`](https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/tree/main/notes).

- what I have already said about coding agents, and the live DRC outbreak
  model built with them
- what my teaching and grants say about the other AI methods, and what the
  literature says about foundation models, universal differential
  equations, and flows in epidemiology
- my record of communicating with government, the public, and other
  scientists during COVID-19
- what the other speakers work on, and so what this workshop means by AI
- a timeline of the outbreaks I have worked on or watched

The style notes were carried over from the JuliaCon 2026 build, including
the catalogue of LLM phrasing I strip out of my own slides.
The [commit history](https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/commits/main) is
the record of what happened next.
